topics.titleTr: Bir Günde Bir Aylık İçerik Üret
topics.titleEn: Batch a Month of Content in a Single Day
topics.angle: checklist + stop posting daily and batch a month of content in one focused session
topics.brief: Contrarian, checklist-driven system against daily scramble. Sections: why daily improvisation kills consistency and quality; the batching workflow (pillars, ideation, scripting, filming, editing, scheduling as separate blocks); repurposing one long asset into many short ones; an AI-assisted step for outlines and captions; a scheduler and a simple content calendar. Key claims to verify: batching and repurposing raise output consistency; a small set of content pillars outperforms random posting. Sources: 2026 creator workflow guides; repurposing case studies. End with a one-day batching checklist and calendar template.

topics.titleTr: ChatGPT Pulse: İşe Yarayan Günlük Özet
topics.titleEn: ChatGPT Pulse: A Daily Briefing That Helps
topics.angle: how-to + set up ChatGPT Pulse so its proactive morning briefing is useful, not noise
topics.brief: Question-driven how-to on proactive AI. Sections: what Pulse is (overnight 'proactive research' surfaced as morning cards from chats, memory and optional connectors); enabling it and connecting Gmail/Calendar safely (connectors off by default); training it with thumbs up/down and topic feedback; privacy and what to keep off; whether a proactive briefing beats an on-demand prompt. Key claims to verify: Pulse synthesizes overnight from memory and feedback; connectors are opt-in; availability is plan-gated. Sources: OpenAI Pulse materials; hands-on Pulse guides. End with a first-week tuning checklist.

topics.titleTr: AI Öğretmenle Her Beceriyi Daha Hızlı Öğren
topics.titleEn: Learn Any Skill Faster With an AI Tutor
topics.angle: guide + turn ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini into a real tutor for any non-coding skill
topics.brief: Story-led guide beyond coding. Sections: setting up a tutor persona and a learning plan; the Feynman loop (explain back, get corrected); spaced-repetition and quizzing prompts; using NotebookLM/Projects to ground lessons in real sources; avoiding the confident-but-wrong trap with verification. Key claims to verify: active recall and spaced repetition beat passive reading; grounding answers in your own sources cuts hallucination; AI tutoring works across languages and skills. Sources: learning-science summaries; AI-study-tool guides. End with a reusable 'be my tutor' prompt template.

topics.titleEn: Beat Procrastination With Systems That Stick
topics.angle: mistakes + why willpower-based fixes fail and which systems actually survive a bad week
topics.brief: Contrarian, mistakes-first take. Sections: why motivation and willpower tactics fail; procrastination as emotion regulation, not laziness; systems that survive contact with reality (tiny first steps, implementation intentions, friction design, time-boxing); the tool trap (endless setup instead of doing); a recovery ritual for broken streaks. Key claims to verify: procrastination links to mood regulation more than time management; reducing friction and shrinking task size beats motivation hacks. Sources: behavioral-science summaries on procrastination; habit-formation research. End with a five-rule anti-procrastination system.

topics.titleTr: Gemini 3.6 Flash ile Ucuz ve Hızlı AI
topics.titleEn: Building With Gemini 3.6 Flash: Cheap, Fast AI
topics.angle: how-to + build cost-efficient agents on Gemini 3.6 Flash and know when to drop to Flash-Lite
topics.brief: Field-notes build guide. Sections: what changed in Gemini 3.6 Flash (better token efficiency, code/agentic planning, lower price); Flash vs Flash-Lite vs Pro for latency and cost; a routing pattern (Flash-Lite for high-volume subagents, Flash for reasoning-lite tasks, escalate to Pro when needed); wiring it via the Gemini API; measuring cost per task. Key claims to verify: 3.6 Flash improved efficiency and planning at lower cost; Flash-Lite targets high-volume, low-latency automation. Sources: Google Gemini July 2026 blog; Gemini API changelog. End with a model-routing decision table.

topics.titleEn: Build Your First MCP Connector (2026 Spec)
topics.angle: how-to + build and connect a working MCP server against the 2026-07-28 stateless spec
topics.brief: Data-led, hands-on tutorial (assumes MCP basics from our explainer). Sections: what the 2026-07-28 spec changed (stateless core, stronger OAuth/OIDC, versioned extensions for Apps and Tasks); scaffolding a minimal server exposing one tool and one resource; auth and testing; connecting it to Claude and other MCP clients; observability and private network tunnels. Key claims to verify: the 2026-07-28 spec introduces a stateless core and stronger auth; the same server works across MCP-compatible clients. Sources: MCP 2026-07-28 spec; Anthropic connector docs. End with a deploy-and-verify checklist.

topics.titleEn: Local-First Apps and Sync Engines in 2026
topics.angle: deep-dive + decide whether local-first with a sync engine beats a classic client-server app
topics.brief: Contrarian deep-dive. Sections: what local-first means (instant local reads/writes, offline, sync in background); CRDTs vs last-write-wins conflict handling; the 2026 sync-engine landscape and what they take off your plate; where local-first shines (collab editors, field apps) and where it hurts (heavy server auth, huge datasets, strict consistency); migration cost. Key claims to verify: CRDTs enable conflict-free merges; sync engines cut hand-rolled offline code; local-first is a poor fit for strong-consistency, server-authority workloads. Sources: local-first research/essays; a sync-engine's docs. End with a fit-or-skip checklist.

topics.titleEn: HTML You No Longer Need JavaScript For
topics.angle: how-to + replace JS-heavy UI patterns with modern native HTML and platform APIs
topics.brief: Data-led how-to on shipping less JavaScript. Sections: native <dialog> for modals (focus trap, backdrop, Escape); the Popover API and popovertarget for menus/tooltips; CSS anchor positioning; <details> for accordions; when native still needs a little JS. Key claims to verify: <dialog>, Popover API and anchor positioning have broad 2026 browser support; native elements bring accessibility and focus management for free. Sources: MDN and web.dev docs; caniuse tables. End with a 'replace this JS with this HTML' cheat sheet.

topics.titleEn: Database Schema Design: A Practical Guide
topics.angle: guide + design a relational schema that stays fast and sane as the product grows
topics.brief: Field-notes guide (pairs with our indexing and migrations posts). Sections: modeling entities and relationships; normalization up to 3NF and when to denormalize deliberately; keys, constraints and foreign keys as correctness guarantees; choosing types (UUID vs bigint, timestamps, enums vs lookup tables); soft deletes, audit columns and JSONB pitfalls; evolving schemas safely. Key claims to verify: constraints prevent whole bug classes; premature denormalization hurts more than it helps; JSONB is powerful but easy to overuse. Sources: PostgreSQL docs; database design references. End with a schema-review checklist.

topics.angle: checklist + run credible on-call and incident response without a big SRE org
topics.brief: Contrarian checklist for teams without a dedicated SRE org. Sections: lightweight on-call that doesn't burn people out; severity levels and a single incident commander; the first 15 minutes (stabilize, communicate, don't debug blindly); blameless postmortems and action items that actually ship; alert hygiene to kill fatigue. Key claims to verify: blameless postmortems improve reliability more than blame; alert fatigue and noisy paging cause missed real incidents; small teams need process, just lighter. Sources: Google SRE book chapters; incident-management guides. End with an incident runbook template.
